stories.headline: Impactful social relationships: A smarter investment for Bangladesh’s youth
stories.summary: Columnist M M Mahbub Hasan proposes “Impactful Social Relationships” (ISR): young people should invest their time and attention as carefully as money, since lost money can be earned again but lost time never returns. He cites the BBS Labour Force Survey 2024 — youth unemployment 8.07% against a national 3.66%, 885,000 of the 2.624 million unemployed being graduates, and 20.3% of youth (about 8.56 million) NEET — arguing purposeful relationships build the skills, confidence and contacts that certificates alone cannot, a youth-employment hook for BCS/Bank.
stories.exam_facts: The columnist illustrates his argument with two fictional but familiar university friends: Rakib spends his evenings at the tea stall and on his phone, while Tania’s small group meets twice a week to learn something new, a teacher has drawn her into research, and she volunteers regularly — so at graduation their certificates are identical but their experience, confidence and contacts are not. He says the causes of youth joblessness are structural — a limited job market, a skills mismatch and social barriers for women — and that solving them is chiefly for the state. The author draws on two decades in development research and banking.
stories.figures: Youth unemployment (ages 15–29) 8.07% vs national 3.66%; graduates 885,000 of 2.624 million unemployed; graduate jobless rate 13.54% (highest by education level); NEET 20.3% of youth, about 8.56 million (BBS Labour Force Survey 2024)
stories.key_people: M M Mahbub Hasan, banker and development researcher (columnist); Rakib and Tania, fictional university friends used as examples in the column
stories.why_it_matters: The 8.07% youth jobless rate, the 13.54% graduate rate and the 20.3% NEET share are the exact BBS 2024 figures BCS/Bank questions ask for on youth unemployment, and they sit alongside the structural causes — a limited job market, skills mismatch and barriers for women — that frame every follow-up story on graduate unemployment.
stories.exam_relevance: Youth unemployment, graduate unemployment, NEET, Labour Force Survey 2024, development and employment policy — core BCS/Bank topics on Bangladesh’s labour market.

stories.headline: Bangladesh raises garment workers' minimum wage 36% after protests
stories.summary: Bangladesh raised garment workers’ minimum wage by 36% — from Tk 12,500 to Tk 17,000 ($139) — on 25 November after weeks of protests since October, the smallest rise in more than a decade. Workers had demanded Tk 30,000 ($240), saying pay lagged food, housing, transport and health costs. The BGMEA put protest losses at $428 million with $254 million of orders shifted abroad; the wage board voted for Tk 17,000 and the rise takes effect in January, feeding BCS/Bank questions on RMG wages and exports.
stories.exam_facts: The garment industry is the world’s second-biggest exporter behind China, accounts for four-fifths of Bangladesh’s export earnings and employs more than four million people. Workers previously got a wage revision every five years, but this time the revision came after three years. On 25 November several hundred protesters set up barricades in Gazipur, some hurling rocks, before police dispersed them with tear gas and stun grenades. Workers’ representative Babul Akhter said workers were “not completely satisfied” but the outcome was “not entirely bad”; union official Kamrul Hasan said workers accepted the offer, noting medium and small factories could not pay much more. MSN reported the rise as the smallest percentage increase since the sector’s first minimum wage was set in 1986.

stories.key_people: Judge Syed Azad Subhani, chairman of the government-appointed garment industry wage board; Babul Akhter, workers’ representative on the wage board; Kamrul Hasan, senior union official, Ekota Garments Sramik Federation; Al Amin, garment worker in Gazipur; Mahdi Amin, prime minister’s adviser on labour
stories.why_it_matters: The Tk 17,000 figure, the 36% rise and the Tk 30,000 demand are the numbers for BCS/Bank questions on RMG wages, and with garments providing four-fifths of export earnings and over four million jobs, every wage round also moves the export and foreign-exchange story.

stories.headline: US unveils proposed tariffs on major partners, including EU and China
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump on 25 November proposed new tariffs on 14 trading partners, including Bangladesh, China, India and the EU, after an eight-month Section 301 probe into alleged excess industrial capacity. China faces the highest rate, 20%, blamed for flooding world markets with cheap steel, electric vehicles and solar products. The duties will not stack on some earlier tariff rounds or exceed negotiated caps, but MSCI’s world stock gauge fell 0.5% — a trade-policy and export question for BCS/Bank.
stories.exam_facts: The 14 partners named are Bangladesh, Cambodia, the European Union, India, Indonesia, Japan, South Korea, Malaysia, Singapore, Switzerland, Taiwan, Thailand, Vietnam and China; Mexico and Norway are excluded from the new levies. The duties would not apply to about $30 billion of Chinese imports the US is considering for tariff reductions, but would add to roughly 25% tariffs on China from Trump’s first term, and would not exceed a 20% cap for China under a year-old truce due to expire on 10 January. A Reuters/Ipsos poll found 62% of respondents would support repealing the tariffs, and Trump has said he plans to rebuild duties the US Supreme Court struck down in February. Note: a separate Prothom Alo headline put the number of partners at 16, against 14 in the main report and the Dhaka Tribune headline. China’s Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun called overcapacity “a false issue”.
stories.figures: 14 trading partners; China up to 20%; about $30 billion of Chinese imports under consideration for tariff reductions; first-term China tariffs about 25%; MSCI world stocks down 0.5%; 62% in Reuters/Ipsos poll back repealing tariffs; 8-month Section 301 probe
stories.key_people: Donald Trump, President of the United States; Xi Jinping, President of China; Guo Jiakun, spokesperson, Chinese Foreign Ministry

stories.headline: Bangladesh Bank reserve heist probe report deferred for 100th time
stories.summary: A Dhaka court deferred the Bangladesh Bank reserve heist probe report for the 100th time on 25 November, after the CID failed to submit it; Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate Jashita Islam set 30 December as the next date. Hackers stole $81 million from Bangladesh Bank’s account with the US Federal Reserve on 5 February 2016, and the CID has investigated ever since the court handed it the case on 16 March 2016 — a banking, cybercrime and money-laundering staple for BCS/Bank.
stories.exam_facts: The case was filed on 15 March 2016 by Zobayer Bin Huda, then deputy director of Bangladesh Bank’s Accounts and Budgeting Department, at Motijheel Police Station under the Money Laundering Prevention Act, against unidentified individuals. The stolen money is believed to have been laundered with the help of a network operating within the country. The deferment was confirmed by Ruknuzzaman, a sub-inspector of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police’s prosecution division.

stories.headline: Sparking the grid: Readiness challenges of the operating organisation of Rooppur NPP
stories.summary: Columnist Mohammad Shawkat Akbar argues Bangladesh’s entry into the “global nuclear club” now depends on the readiness of Rooppur’s operating organisation, after Power Unit 1 reached initial criticality and entered Stage C of power start-up commissioning, clearing the way for first trial supply and first grid connection. He warns starting a reactor is like “riding a tiger” — irreversible once critical — and says 80% of the nuclear system lies beneath the surface, in safety, security, logistics and governance.
stories.exam_facts: The columnist says keeping the reactor under control requires flawless trial runs and secure provisional acceptance of the power unit from the vendor or general contractor, verifying all technical and economic metrics against the plant’s design. He says the plant’s survival depends on an institutional ecosystem: a specialised government body (NEPIO), a strictly independent national nuclear regulator, and the plant operating organisation, all sustained by expert Technical Support Organisations (TSOs). He says the operating organisation carries the heaviest responsibility for safety and sustainability throughout the plant’s decades-long lifecycle. Note: the collected body text was truncated at 4,000 characters, so the column’s later sections were not available to this writer.

stories.headline: Hasina's return plan, extradition separate issues, says India's MEA
stories.summary: India's foreign ministry said on 25 November that Sheikh Hasina's reported plan to return voluntarily to Bangladesh and Dhaka's request for her extradition are two separate matters. MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said the extradition request is being examined under established procedures, while a citizen returning voluntarily with travel documents is a different issue. Hasina fled to India on 5 August 2024 and was sentenced to death on 17 November 2025; a Reuters report said she planned to return on 16 December.
stories.exam_facts: Hasina requested a Biman Bangladesh Airlines aircraft to bring her home from Delhi, according to the Reuters report cited by Prothom Alo. Prime Minister's Adviser Zahed Ur Rahman said on Tuesday the matter would be discussed with India. Jaiswal said India had no role in the question of whether she would be brought back in handcuffs, calling it a matter between Bangladesh's former prime minister and its current government. Jaiswal also said attacks on Hindu minorities in Bangladesh, including in Narail and Pabna, were a matter of concern and urged thorough investigation; Narail district police said Facebook reports of vandalism in Bendar Char village were false and fabricated and that there are no Hindu settlements there.
stories.figures: Fled to India 5 August 2024; death sentence 17 November 2025; reported return date 16 December; MEA briefing 25 November 2026
stories.key_people: Randhir Jaiswal, spokesperson, India's Ministry of External Affairs; Sheikh Hasina, former prime minister of Bangladesh; Zahed Ur Rahman, Prime Minister's Adviser
stories.why_it_matters: The MEA's separation of voluntary return from extradition, and the 17 November 2025 death sentence under the existing extradition treaty, are the exact facts for BCS questions on Bangladesh-India relations, extradition and the July uprising trials.

stories.headline: Turkish Sanko, local DBL to invest $300m in denim plant, create 4,400 jobs
stories.summary: Turkish conglomerate Sanko Holding and Bangladesh's DBL Group will jointly invest $300 million in an export-oriented denim plant at Sreehatta Economic Zone in Moulvibazar, with an integrated spinning unit. The plant will produce about 10 million metres of denim fabric a month and create about 4,400 direct jobs, with commercial operations expected in the first quarter of 2028. Sanko's family shareholders will own 49% and DBL Group 51%.
stories.exam_facts: The Sanko delegation was led by Vice Chairman Fatih Konukoglu and board member Hakan Konukoglu, and met Invest Bangladesh Chairman Ashik Chowdhury in Dhaka on 25 November, accompanied by DBL Group Managing Director MA Jabbar. Jabbar said construction would start soon, with the Turkish partner contributing manufacturing technology and technical expertise, and that most jobs would go to Bangladeshi workers. Denim requires heavy investment in machinery, technology, skilled manpower and production efficiency, and the plant is meant to bring international textile technology into Bangladesh's backward linkage industry.

stories.headline: Prime Bank, Lloyds and Enigio take UK-Bangladesh digital trade to everyday scale
stories.summary: Prime Bank PLC, Lloyds and Enigio have completed multiple cross-border documentary collections for apparel shipments from Bangladesh to the UK, entirely in digital form — documents prepared and transferred in under an hour, and the full process done in 48 hours end to end. The step takes UK-Bangladesh digital trade to everyday scale, moving the corridor's trade documentation from paper to routine digital use. For BCS/Bank, it is the exam's live example of digital trade finance: banks in two countries settling trade documents without paper.
stories.exam_facts: The collections covered apparel shipments by Bangladeshi manufacturer Viyellatex Limited to a UK garment wholesaler; Prime Bank prepared and transferred the documents to Lloyds in under an hour using Enigio's trace:original solution, and the full process took 48 hours from creation of the digital documents in Bangladesh to release to the buyer. No original paper documents or courier services were used. The collections ran under the ICC's Uniform Rules for Collections (URC 522) and electronic URC, with the concurrence of Bangladesh Bank and under the UK Electronic Trade Documents Act 2023. Lloyds had completed its first digital trade transaction between Bangladesh and the UK earlier in November 2026.
stories.figures: Documents prepared and transferred in under an hour; full process 48 hours end to end; apparel shipments by Viyellatex Limited to a UK garment wholesaler.
stories.key_people: Faisal Rahman, Managing Director and CEO of Prime Bank; Surath Sengupta, Managing Director of Transaction Banking Products at Lloyds.
stories.why_it_matters: Multiple fully digital documentary collections on the Bangladesh-UK corridor, taken to everyday scale, are the concrete case for BCS/Bank questions on digital trade finance and paperless trade.

stories.headline: Dhaka seeks water-flow guarantee as Ganges treaty nears expiry
stories.summary: Bangladesh has called for a guaranteed water-flow provision in a new Ganges water-sharing agreement with India, as the 30-year treaty signed on 12 December 1996 expires on 12 December with no formal negotiations yet under way. Dhaka wants a guarantee clause like the 1977 agreement's, under which it received at least 80% of its stipulated share in any 10-day period of low flow. Water Resources Minister Md Shahid Uddin Chowdhury Anee said Bangladesh is ready for talks and has written to his Indian counterpart.
stories.exam_facts: Under the 1996 treaty, water is allocated every 10 days on Farakka flow: at 70,000 cusecs or less the two countries share it equally; between 70,000 and 75,000 cusecs Bangladesh receives 35,000 cusecs; at 75,000 cusecs or more India receives 40,000 cusecs and Bangladesh the rest. Flows are monitored at Farakka Barrage and Hardinge Bridge from 1 January to 31 May each year. The 91st Joint Rivers Commission meeting in Dhaka finalised the 2026 annual implementation report but did not discuss renewal. Bangladesh proposed negotiations in June, India sought a technical committee in August, and the minister wrote again on 17 November; a high-level technical committee led by Prime Minister's Adviser Professor Rashed Al Mahmud Titumir is preparing for talks.

stories.headline: Bangladesh's GDP growth hits 25-year low of 3.2% amid mounting economic woes
stories.summary: Bangladesh's GDP growth has fallen to 3.2%, reportedly its lowest in more than 25 years, amid rising inflation and disruptions in industrial production, according to an article in Dhaka-based The Daily Star reported by National Herald. Weak remittances, sluggish exports, low foreign direct investment, tax evasion and banking-sector stress are worsening the pressure. Revenue collection in the first quarter of the current fiscal year fell short of target by Tk 42,000 crore, while the 2026-27 budget projects a deficit of Tk 2,00,000 crore.
stories.exam_facts: The article flags inflated costs of mega projects, rising non-performing loans in the banking sector and a credit crunch in industrial financing, and says inadequate FDI has constrained employment generation, industrial investment and export growth. It says bridging the fiscal gap could prove difficult given structural and administrative weaknesses of the National Board of Revenue, and calls for realistic budgeting of capital projects, cuts in unproductive and revenue expenditure and improvements in governance. It also notes the prime minister's decision to cut personal expenditure as a possible signal of fiscal discipline.

stories.headline: Climate justice is gender justice: Why climate action must address gender-based violence
stories.summary: Columnist Farhana Afroz argues that climate justice is also gender justice: climate action that overlooks gender inequality cannot deliver inclusive or sustainable resilience. She writes that climate shocks disrupt livelihoods, displace families and weaken the support systems protecting women and girls, raising their exposure to violence and exploitation. She cites the BBS-UNFPA Violence Against Women Survey 2024: 81% of ever-married women in disaster-prone areas had experienced violence by their husbands in their lifetime, against 74% in non-disaster-prone areas.
stories.exam_facts: The columnist writes on the eve of the 16 Days of Activism against Gender-Based Violence. She argues that when families lose homes and income, women face greater financial dependency and unpaid care responsibilities, and that displacement and unsafe living conditions increase exposure to violence, exploitation and abuse. An International Rescue Committee assessment in southern Bangladesh found 66.9% of women and girls did not feel comfortable using cyclone shelters because of safety and facility-related concerns.

stories.summary: Dhaka's security guards work long shifts for modest wages, the TBS feature reports: Murad Ali, 44, a guard at a Chinese restaurant in Mirpur, earns Tk 8,000 a month plus Tk 3,000-4,000 from a share of restaurant sales and Tk 2,000 extra for sweeping and mopping, working from 6:30am with a three-hour break. stories.headline: Trump unveils new tariffs over excess industrial capacity, undeterred by midterms defeat
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump fired a new tariff salvo on Wednesday on 14 major trading partners, including China, Japan and the European Union, undeterred by his Republican Party's midterm losses. His administration proposed new maximum potential rates of 20% to 40% to counter excess industrial capacity, though the USTR said it intends to cap duties at lower levels agreed under trade deals. The move follows an eight-month Section 301 investigation and aims to rebuild tariff leverage after the Supreme Court struck down Trump's broad global duties in February.
stories.exam_facts: The USTR separately proposed a new 10% tariff on imports of Brazil's finished Embraer commercial aircraft and higher duties on Brazilian sugar imports above quotas, to push Brasilia to rectify alleged trade problems. The effort seeks to put Trump's tariffs on more solid legal and political ground by backing them with Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974, described as a court-tested trade law, and addresses foreign subsidies and industrial policies viewed as major trade problems by both Republicans and Democrats. Note the figures differ between sources: CA03 reports the highest proposed rate as 20% for China, while this story reports maximum potential rates of 20% to 40%, with the USTR saying applied rates will be capped lower under trade deals.
stories.figures: 14 trading partners; maximum potential tariff rates 20%-40%; 8-month Section 301 investigation; Supreme Court struck down broad global duties in February 2026; Brazil: new 10% tariff on Embraer aircraft, higher duties on sugar above quotas
stories.key_people: Donald Trump, US President; US Trade Representative (USTR)
stories.why_it_matters: The 20-40% maximum-potential range, the Section 301 legal basis and the separate Brazil Embraer and sugar tariffs are the distinct facts for BCS questions on US protectionism, and they sit alongside CA03's 20% ceiling for China, so the two stories must be read together.
stories.exam_relevance: US tariffs, Section 301, WTO/trade policy, US-China trade, Bangladesh's export exposure - core BCS international affairs and economy topics.

mcqs.question: According to the Labour Force Survey 2024 cited in the article, what share of young people in Bangladesh are NEET — in neither education, employment nor training?
mcqs.explanation: The survey shows 20.3 per cent of young people, roughly 8.56 million, are NEET; 8.07% is the youth unemployment rate and 13.54% is the graduate jobless rate.

mcqs.question: What is the new minimum monthly wage fixed for garment workers?
mcqs.explanation: The wage board fixed Tk 17,000, up 36% from Tk 12,500; workers had demanded Tk 30,000, and their representatives voted for Tk 18,000.

mcqs.question: Which country faces the highest proposed new US tariff rate of 20 per cent?
mcqs.explanation: The highest rate of 20 per cent would hit China, which Washington blames for flooding world markets with cheap exports.

mcqs.question: How many times has the submission of the investigation report in the Bangladesh Bank reserve heist case now been deferred?
mcqs.explanation: The report's submission was deferred once again, marking the 100th postponement; the court set 30 December as the next date.

mcqs.question: Which stage of power start-up commissioning has Power Unit 1 of the Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant entered?
mcqs.explanation: Power Unit 1 has officially entered Stage C of its power start-up commissioning after successfully achieving initial criticality.

mcqs.question: When did Sheikh Hasina flee to India after being ousted from power?
mcqs.explanation: Hasina fled to India on 5 August 2024; on 17 November 2025, International Crimes Tribunal-1 sentenced her to death.

mcqs.question: How many direct jobs is the planned Sanko–DBL denim factory expected to create?
mcqs.explanation: The $300 million factory at Sreehatta Economic Zone will produce about 10 million metres of denim a month and create about 4,400 direct jobs.

mcqs.question: Which three organisations completed multiple cross-border documentary collections between Bangladesh and the UK entirely in digital form?

options.B: Lloyds, Standard Chartered and Prime Bank

mcqs.explanation: Prime Bank PLC, Lloyds and Enigio completed multiple cross-border documentary collections between Bangladesh and the UK, entirely in digital form.

mcqs.question: When is the 30-year Ganges water-sharing treaty set to expire?
mcqs.explanation: The treaty, signed on 12 December 1996, is set to expire on December 12, and Bangladesh is seeking a guaranteed water-flow provision in a new agreement.

mcqs.question: According to the article, Bangladesh's GDP growth has hit a 25-year low of what?
mcqs.explanation: GDP growth has hit a 25-year low of 3.2% amid weak remittances, sluggish exports, low FDI, tax evasion and banking-sector stress.

mcqs.question: According to the BBS-UNFPA Violence Against Women Survey 2024, what share of ever-married women in disaster-prone areas had experienced violence by their husbands during their lifetime?
mcqs.explanation: The survey found 81% of ever-married women in disaster-prone areas had experienced violence by their husbands, compared with 74% in non-disaster-prone areas.

mcqs.question: What is security guard Murad Ali's monthly salary at the Chinese restaurant in Mirpur?
mcqs.explanation: Murad's salary is Tk 8,000, with Tk 3,000–4,000 more from a share of restaurant sales; Tk 16,000 is fellow guard Mushfiq's pay.

mcqs.question: How many trading partners did the US propose new tariffs on, including Bangladesh, China and the EU?
mcqs.explanation: The administration proposed levies on 14 trading partners to combat what it calls structural excess industrial capacity.

mcqs.question: What does 'morale' mean in the sentence 'who silently drains their time and morale'?

options.B: A large sum of money saved for the future
options.C: A formal written agreement between friends

mcqs.explanation: Morale means confidence, enthusiasm and mental strength; here, bad company drains a young person's time and morale.

mcqs.question: What does 'provocation' mean?

options.A: A peaceful settlement of a dispute
options.B: An act meant to stir anger or trouble
options.C: A government order closing a factory
options.D: A formal apology issued after a protest

mcqs.explanation: Provocation means an act intended to provoke anger or unrest; the union leader warned workers not to be influenced by propaganda, provocation or misinformation.

mcqs.question: In 'the garment industry is Bangladesh's economic lifeline', what does 'lifeline' mean?

options.A: A rope used by sailors to climb a ship
options.B: A new law that protects factory owners from closure
options.C: Something vital that keeps the economy alive
options.D: A loan taken from a foreign bank

mcqs.explanation: A lifeline is something essential for survival; garments account for four-fifths of Bangladesh's export earnings.

mcqs.question: What does 'retaliation' mean in 'stopped short of threatening retaliation'?

options.A: A public apology for a trade dispute
options.B: A request for new trade talks
options.C: A promise to lower import duties

mcqs.explanation: Retaliation means striking back; Beijing dismissed overcapacity claims but did not threaten to hit back with its own tariffs.

mcqs.question: What does 'undeterred' mean in 'undeterred in his protectionist push'?
mcqs.explanation: Undeterred means not put off; Trump pressed ahead with new tariffs despite his party's midterm losses.

mcqs.question: What is 'protectionism'?

options.A: Free trade with no import duties at all
options.C: A ban on all exports from a country
options.D: A system of fixed exchange rates

mcqs.explanation: Protectionism is the policy of protecting home industries from foreign competition through tariffs and other barriers.

mcqs.question: What does 'postponement' mean in 'marking the 100th postponement'?

options.A: The final approval of a report
options.B: The public release of secret documents
options.C: Putting something off to a later date
options.D: The arrest of a suspect in a case

mcqs.explanation: Postponement means delaying to a later time; the CID again failed to submit the reserve-heist probe report, the 100th delay.

mcqs.question: What does 'heist' mean in 'the Bangladesh Bank reserve heist case'?

options.B: A court order to freeze accounts
options.C: An official audit of foreign reserves

mcqs.explanation: A heist is a major robbery; hackers stole $81 million from Bangladesh Bank's account with the US Federal Reserve in February 2016.

mcqs.question: What does 'commissioning' mean in 'Stage C of its power start-up commissioning'?

options.A: Bringing a new plant into operation
options.B: A tax charged on electricity sales
options.C: A meeting of the plant's safety committee
options.D: The sale of a power plant to a private buyer

mcqs.explanation: Commissioning is the testing and start-up process that brings a new plant into service; Rooppur Unit 1 has entered Stage C after initial criticality.

mcqs.question: What does 'provisional' mean in 'secure provisional acceptance of the power unit'?
mcqs.explanation: Provisional means temporary or conditional; the plant needs secure provisional acceptance from the vendor before full operation.

mcqs.question: What does 'in response to' mean in 'made the remarks in response to questions from journalists'?

options.D: In place of a formal request

mcqs.explanation: 'In response to' means as a reply or reaction to something; the MEA spokesperson spoke in response to journalists' questions.

mcqs.question: What does 'on the eve of' mean in 'On the eve of the 16 Days of Activism against Gender-Based Violence'?

options.A: Long after the event has ended
options.B: During the middle of the event

mcqs.explanation: 'On the eve of' means just before something happens; the article was written just before the 16 Days of Activism campaign.
